title: Space simulation by an arithmetic register program
statement: Let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, let $A$ be an arithmetic register program with a finite state set, and choose an initial state $l_0$. For each of the finitely many oracle languages $A_j$, let $s_j$ be a space bound, and suppose each $A_j$ is decidable in space $s_j$. Let $S,W:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $C\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $1\le S(n)$ and $W(n)\le C S(n)$ for every $n$, and suppose $s_j(v)\le C S(n)$ whenever $v\le 2n+2+m(2W(n)+2)$. If, on every input $x$, the program started in state $l_0$ with all registers zero halts with the answer deciding membership in $L$, and throughout the run every register has a canonical binary representation of length at most $W(|x|)$ while the stated step preconditions hold, then $L$ is decidable in space $O(S(n))$ (equivalently, $L\in\mathrm{SPACE}(S)$).
hypotheses_covered: Finite state set and decidable equality
Each oracle language has a decider using space at most $s_j$
Functions $S,W$ and constant $C$ are natural-number valued
$s_j(v)\le C S(n)$ under the stated bound on $v$
On every input, the specified initial run halts with the indicator of membership in $L$
At every time before halting, the precondition holds and each encoded register value plus one has bit-length at most $W(|x|)$
